placement: After the information-package-creation UpdateAttribute; success relationship routes to Add event.groovy. This is the final event-emitting step in the flow.
purpose: Stages event.* and agent.* attributes so Add event.groovy emits a 'transfer' NDJSON record covering extraction out of the legacy SAM-FS archive + DPX fixity verification. SIP creation is now its own event (information package creation) and is no longer mentioned here.

properties.event.detail: Pakke hentet ut av Nasjonalbibliotekets eldre arkivlager Oracle HSM (SAM-FS) for rearkivering; integritet bekreftet ved at DPX-sjekksummer ble verifisert mot SAM-FS-metadata med md5sum (GNU coreutils).
properties.agent.name: Apache NiFi
properties.agent.note: Programvare for automatisering av dataflyter som muliggjør utforming og administrasjon av komplekse datapipelines.

notes: event.datetime references the dedicated transfer.event.datetime attribute (set to the fetch-end time in '04_Set fetch.end, fetch.duration, package.size.start.groovy'), not the generic event.datetime — which later stages (e.g. RAWcooked migration) overwrite. This event is emitted last in the flow, so it needs a timestamp captured back when the SAM-FS extraction actually finished, otherwise it would appear out of order relative to the migration event.

All four agent.* properties are set explicitly even though they match the defaults in Add event.groovy. This makes the agent unambiguous from the NiFi UI alone and protects against agent attribute leakage from upstream processors (e.g. RAWcooked sets agent.name=RAWcooked on the flowfile; NiFi doesn't clear flowfile attributes between processors, so without an explicit override the appender would pick those up and produce a transfer event credited to RAWcooked).

If the default values in Add event.groovy ever drift (NiFi version bump, agentNote rewording), update this processor in lockstep — the defaults and these values describe the same agent and must stay aligned.
